column7: F3d: both core.UpdateRole's and core.CreateRole's final GetRolePermissions call (building the response's permission list) ran AFTER their own storage.WithTransaction committed and after audit logging -- a fault there reported an ERROR to the caller while the role update/create and its audit trail had already committed (oracle (a): AuditEvent table differs). Found live by an unattended fuzz burst smoke-testing coverage batch 6's two new /system ops (it found this instead, one call further down the already-fixed UpdateRole path); CreateRole had the structurally identical gap, fixed proactively before a second live finding. Fixed by moving each function's final GetRolePermissions read to be the LAST statement inside its own storage.WithTransaction closure, so a fault there rolls the whole operation back instead of reporting error-after-commit. Proving test is the fuzz harness itself -- corpus entry 637f47f4387c3138 is the permanent regression; see docs/findings/2026-09-21-FINDING-role-update-permission-replace-swallows-storage-errors.md. Regression-corpus fidelity note (2026-09-27): ADR-108 Phase 6 step 14c's opCatalog shrink (removing 7 /system-proxy-only ops) silently retargeted this corpus file's decoded operation from "REST POST /api/v1/rotation-policies/" to an unrelated op -- repaired by re-encoding the file's byte[0] to the same op's new index, verified to decode back to the original op/method/NthCall/kind tuple; guarded going forward by TestOpcatalogCorpusFilesTargetPinnedOps (server/faultops/opcatalog_corpus_pin_test.go).
